close_reason: Parity suite: 171s cold / 6-17s warm, no FUSE, but needs full dev shell which today's CI cannot build; a gate needs a slim CI shell + cached cells
description:
## Question

How long does `src/cmd/check-test-runner-parity` take on a warm and a cold machine, what does it need (buck2 daemon, nix store paths, network, FUSE/macFUSE), and could it run in the repo's existing GitHub Actions setup (`.github/workflows/*`) on the runners those use? Answer with the facts a 'CI gate or manual checklist step' decision needs.

comments.text: Answer: the suite is fast, and it does not need FUSE. It cannot run in today's GitHub Actions CI. With the dev shell already built, it takes about 3 min cold (fresh buck-out and daemon, warm nix store; 171s on an M5 Max) and 6-17 s warm. It runs 6 buck2 test //... calls; all 3 scenarios match on 30 targets. It needs the full dev shell (buck2, tk, python3, the rust/go/python/ts/solidity toolchains), nix-store cells, and a buck2 daemon that starts itself. It needs the network only to fill a cold store. No FUSE, turnkey-composed or macFUSE: cells are nix-store symlinks, and test targets compile composition without the fuse features. Blockers for CI: (1) CI removed every job that enters the full dev shell because of disk and time limits (b64b124: jj built from source, 40+ min, out of disk); (2) turnkey-composed is in toolchain.toml, and its nix package cannot build on ubuntu (no pkg-config/fuse3 for fuser's libfuse feature) or on macOS runners (needs macFUSE); (3) about 5.1 GB of closure plus uncached cells plus 2.5 GB of buck-out against the runner's 14 GB SSD. To make it a gate: a slim CI shell without turnkey-composed, jj, mdbook or beadwork; cells in Cachix; a path-filtered job on ubuntu-latest. Otherwise it stays the manual step that the buck2-source.nix header already prescribes. Findings on local bookmark research/parity-suite-ci-gate, docs/research/parity-suite-ci-gate.md
Findings landed on main in 827682bc (docs/research/); the research/* bookmark was deleted.

title: Is the test-runner parity suite fast and self-contained enough to be a CI gate?
